item.title: [github_trending] morluto/rea
item.description: rea is a GitHub project that applies agents to reverse engineering, spanning app behaviour analysis all the way down to native binaries. Rather than being a single-purpose disassembler, it aims to let autonomous agents drive the investigation, which makes it relevant to security researchers and anyone who needs to understand closed-source software.

item.title: [juejin] Cursor 转 Codex 大半个月，聊聊我的真实感受
item.description: A developer recounts a year on Cursor, praising its Tab completion, Cmd+K, Agent and Plan Mode, and notes he once shipped a mini-program without writing code. In April 2026 Cursor moved from fixed licenses to usage-based billing, so his company switched its China region to OpenAI Codex. He finds Codex closer to a general-purpose super Agent than to an IDE.

item.title: [36kr] 免费洗衣、洗车、还报销车费，现在的网吧到底有多狠？
item.description: The headline claims some internet cafes now offer free laundry and car washing, and even reimburse customers' taxi fares. The linked page isn't summarized here; details beyond the title, such as pricing or how such a business model works, aren't available, so the claim can't be verified.

item.title: [infoq] 黄仁勋为微软站台：没有 Windows 就不会有英伟达，Satya 当场“讨市值”
item.description: At its October 8 Windows event, Microsoft introduced "hybrid intelligence": model routing and Windows ML let GitHub Copilot and other products switch between cloud and local models, and GitHub Copilot's HydraFusion will call local models running on Windows PCs directly. Jensen Huang and Satya Nadella traced the partnership from Windows 95, DirectX and CUDA to Azure's InfiniBand HPC, arguing agents are becoming a new kind of computer user. Microsoft shares rose roughly 0.1% that day.

item.title: [v2ex] [分享创造] 做了一个不需要服务器就能托管 git 仓库的私人服务
item.description: gits is a git hosting service that runs entirely on Cloudflare's serverless offerings, so it needs no server of your own, and its bundled GitHub App syncs every repository under an authorized account. It deliberately omits issues and pull requests, keeping only plain repo hosting — useful for repositories you'd rather not put on GitHub, or for backing up private ones.

item.title: [juejin] 面试官问你：“AI 能写 80% 的代码了，公司为什么还需要你？”
item.description: This post examines a now-common 2026 interview question: if AI writes 80% of the code, why is the company still hiring you? It argues the stock answers — AI's code quality is poor, AI doesn't understand requirements, someone has to do code review — no longer land, and suggests answering on two levels: AI writes code while humans make decisions, and AI writes a file while humans design a system.

item.title: [infoq] CLAUDE.md 还是 AGENTS.md？Anthropic 的答案是：以后都不用
item.description: The Claude Code team has confirmed it will support AGENTS.md, the instruction-file standard it previously refused to adopt, a stance that drew a public warning from Shopify CEO Tobi Lütke. On the Latent Space podcast, core team member Thariq Shihipar went further: as models get stronger, static instruction files like CLAUDE.md may eventually become unnecessary, so new projects can skip them until the same failure keeps recurring.

item.title: [36kr] AI“克隆”的Adobe全家桶一夜爆火，但先别急着卸载正版
item.description: A 36Kr piece looks at an AI tool that mimics the Adobe suite and went viral overnight, with the author cautioning users not to uninstall their legitimate Adobe software just yet. The linked page isn't summarized here; details beyond the title aren't available.

item.title: [v2ex] [Apple] 网易云音乐能跨区更新不
item.description: A V2EX user in the Apple section asks whether NetEase Cloud Music can still be updated across App Store regions, noting the app is no longer downloadable in the Hong Kong store while the US store's status is unclear. It's essentially a query about how widely the app has been pulled and how existing users should handle future updates.

item.title: [v2ex] [Claude] 凌晨 4 点失眠了
item.description: A V2EX user posted at 4 a.m. after spending the whole night trying to top up a Claude subscription with Japan-region gift cards; the payment eventually went through, with the 3,000-yen tier working out to roughly a 5% discount at current exchange rates. He jokes about how much energy he burns just to keep using Claude.

item.title: [infoq] Rails 之父 DHH 狂吹 Rust 快 150 倍，被开发者翻代码后群嘲
item.description: At Rails World 2026, DHH called Rust the ugliest programming language of the past 40 years, yet said he loves it as long as agents write the code and he never has to read it. He had agents rewrite 37signals' Campfire chat app in Elixir, Go and Rust; loading a chat room page, Rust hit 36,260 requests per second, roughly 150x Rails, 50x Elixir and 9.4x Go.

item.title: [v2ex] [推广] Qwen Image 2.1 Pro 与 Nano Banana 2.1：透明编辑、视频参考和多轮修图怎么选？
item.description: This sponsored comparison pits Qwen Image 2.1 Pro against Nano Banana 2.1 for image work: Qwen takes up to 10 reference images and focuses on transparent assets and masked local edits, with no web search, while Nano Banana 2.1 supports multi-turn conversational retouching, video references and Google search, accepts up to 14 reference images, and outputs at 1K, 2K or 4K. It's aimed at creators deciding between extracting transparent subjects, iterating on one image, or grounding visuals in searc

item.title: [v2ex] [分享创造] [开源自荐] 小喷 1.1.0： Mac 菜单栏语音伙伴，支持 ChatGPT 订阅和本机 Ollama
item.description: Xiaopeng (小喷) is a native macOS menu-bar voice assistant written in Swift 6 and SwiftUI and released under MIT; say its wake word to check weather, set timers or change volume without hunting for a chat window. Version 1.1.0 adds echo cancellation and barge-in, parses reminder and volume commands locally, and can use your own OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible API, a ChatGPT subscription or local Ollama. It needs macOS 14+ on Apple Silicon, and the unsigned build lacks Apple notarization.

item.title: [infoq] OpenAI 只用 15 天，就杀死了估值 100 亿美元的 Jev？
item.description: At its DevDay, OpenAI introduced a Decisions API built on GPT-6 Luna, its smallest and cheapest model, which picks from preset options and returns a confidence score. OpenAI cites 150ms latency versus 1.6 seconds for calling Luna directly on the same task. It's in limited preview with pricing and option counts undisclosed, and closely mirrors the core capability of Jev, which launched just 15 days earlier — prompting a "Jev Is Dead" thread on Reddit.

item.title: [infoq] 单次RL后训练烧掉260万美元、每步37亿Token，小米披露MiMo-V2.6“规模化强化学习”路线
item.description: Xiaomi's MiMo team published a technical report on MiMo-V2.6, releasing two sparse MoE models: Pro (1.02T total, 42B active) and Flash (310B, 15B active). Its scaled agentic RL pipeline samples 1,568 prompts per step with 16 rollouts each, roughly 25,000 trajectories and 2.7–3.7 billion tokens, using GRPO with asynchronous partial rollouts. RL post-training costs about $2.6M for Pro and $0.9M for Flash, with Grader compute at 12.7% and 14.2%.

item.title: [infoq] 比 Astra 还贵！GPT-6.1 Sol 极速版上线，社区吐槽：“500 美元套餐都撑不过一天”
item.description: On October 8, OpenAI added an Ultrafast service tier to GPT-6.1 Sol, the model it shipped on September 29, in the Responses API; developers keep the same model name and just set the tier to ultrafast. Positioned as its fastest API tier, it is priced at six times the standard per-token rate and targets latency-sensitive workloads willing to pay more for speed.

item.title: [v2ex] [分享创造] 做了个 Nano Banana 图片生成站：从一句脑洞，到产品图、海报和社媒配图
item.description: A developer shared Nano Banana, a web tool that puts prompt entry, aspect-ratio and resolution selection and result viewing on one page. It supports 1K, 2K and 4K output plus batch generation, costing 8, 12 and 28 credits per image respectively, with the total shown before submission; sample prompts on the homepage load straight into the generator. It targets people making product shots, posters or social images.

item.title: [infoq] 模型开放之后，AI能力为什么仍难以复用？
item.description: An InfoQ article argues that open-sourcing AI models doesn't make their capabilities reusable: a downloadable model isn't a reproducible system, and AI projects depend on weights, data, prompts, tool interfaces and runtime environments, so swapping the base model or a tool can break existing workflows. It points to the 2026 Global Open-source AI competition (GOAI), which drew 91 countries and regions, over 14,000 developers and 2,999 valid entries narrowed to 70 finalists, and notes that docs, e

item.title: [infoq] 金融监管领域的 Harness 实践：让知识与数据驱动 Agent 稳定运行
item.description: Yu Haojun, chief engineer at Zhongruan Rongxin, gave a talk at AICon 2026 Shenzhen on Harness practices in financial regulatory reporting. His approach combines knowledge and data foundations, a controlled state machine, and full-chain traceability to turn free-form agents into strictly governed systems that would rather abstain than answer wrong. The domain demands near-100% accuracy and zero tolerance for error, making it relevant to teams deploying agents in heavily regulated industries.

item.title: [v2ex] [分享发现] 刚刚注册 Muse 成功的方式
item.description: A V2EX user describes a luck-based way to register for Muse: signing in through the cloud browser at browser.lexmount.com with a Google account, then registering with a non-Gmail address, which went through with no verification after several Gmail attempts were blocked. They also share invite code TLM0N7, said to give both parties 1 billion Muse tokens if redeemed in Settings within 48 hours of joining. It's one person's anecdote, not an official method.

item.description: QCon Shanghai runs October 22-24, focused on engineering practice for the Harness AI era and covering AI-native architecture, agent runtime, AI infra, and agent safety and observability. Bilibili engineer Zhang Xinzheng will speak in the AI-driven software engineering track, drawing on backend, web and mobile work to argue that AI cuts code generation costs but not the cost of delivering correctness, and will cover constraints, localization, verification and measurement.

item.title: [hackernews] Whistle: Speech to Text in 16.9 MB
item.description: Whistle is an open speech recognition model that ships in just 16.9 MB and runs on the same CPU engine as Needle. It transcribes seven languages and returns its first token in 11 ms, and since it can load alongside Needle, one binary can turn a clip straight into tool calls — useful for lightweight voice interfaces on local or edge hardware.

item.title: [juejin] 被吹上天的 JWT，为什么主流网站一个都不用
item.description: Using github.com as the example, the author notes its cookies contain just a single _gh_session value — Rails-encrypted session data — to explain why mainstream sites keep state on the server rather than packing it into a JWT. It is aimed at backend developers choosing an authentication strategy and wondering where JWTs actually fall short in production.

item.title: [juejin] 2026编程圈很火的10个Skills
item.description: A Juejin roundup of the ten most popular AI coding-assistant Skills of 2026, built on Anthropic's Agent Skills standard from October 2025, where a Skill is a folder containing a SKILL.md file that Claude loads on demand from ~/.claude/skills/. The author notes 1,400+ Claude Code Skills exist on GitHub but 70% of 100 community Skills tested failed, and the top pick, Superpowers, bundles 20+ workflow submodules.

item.title: [juejin] 三年了，为什么 AI 应用还没爆发？
item.description: Featured on Juejin: 三年了，为什么 AI 应用还没爆发？

item.title: [juejin] 从codex转战workbuddy使用一周的感受
item.description: A long-time Codex user documents a week of switching to WorkBuddy, Tencent's agentic coding tool, covering the pitfalls hit along the way and the money saved. The write-up is explicitly not sponsored and avoids trashing either tool, which makes it worth reading for developers weighing a migration and wondering what it really costs.

item.title: [juejin] 再见 Superpowers！很多 Skill 真的可以扔掉了。
item.description: With models like GPT-5.6, K3 and Claude Fable5 now able to read a project, trace call chains and add tests on their own, the author argues most development Skills that merely restate routine steps can be dropped, using Codex as his example. He also notes Codex's progressive disclosure caps Skill metadata at 2% of the context window or 8,000 characters, so too many Skills compete for attention; he keeps fewer than 20.

item.title: [juejin] 为什么不推荐走Agent开发？
item.description: Writing as Feiyu, the author argues Agent development roles only hold long-term value when the domain itself is growing and driven by real business demand, and predicts most existing Agent jobs will be eliminated within one to two years. He frames Agent work as a branch of backend engineering, saying that a LangChain or LangGraph demo is not enough to land a high-paying offer in today's crowded market.

item.title: [github_trending] boykopovar/AnyPS5
item.description: AnyPS5 converts PS5 executables into Linux and Windows native format via a relinker, plus implementations of system prx libraries suited to dynamic linking, with no emulation or separate runtime process. So far the README lists just one verified title, the 2D platformer Dreaming Sarah, so it is early-stage but worth a look for anyone interested in binary relinking and replacing console system libraries.

item.title: [juejin] AI 时代，最危险的不是被替代，而是努力不沉淀
item.description: A Juejin post argues that with AI one day's work now covers three, but managers know it too, so more and more urgent tasks pile up. The author's warning: the real risk isn't being replaced, but that the extra output never accumulates into portable career assets. He splits AI use into task efficiency, process integration and capability rebuilding, and staying at the first level only makes you a faster executor.

item.title: [juejin] 2026年金九银十，我面了22个前端
item.description: A front-end interviewer recaps the 2026 autumn hiring season: with the team expanding, they worked through more than 30 résumés and ran 22 technical interviews, ending with 3 offers and 2 actual hires. Only that opening is available in the source, so the interview questions and candidate assessments that follow aren't included; relevant to developers preparing for front-end interviews or running hiring loops.

item.title: [github_trending] storytold/artcraft
item.description: ArtCraft, hosted in the GitHub repo storytold/artcraft, describes itself as a crafting engine for artists, designers and filmmakers and brands itself 'The IDE for artists'. Its README links a two-minute demo on YouTube plus Discord, X and LinkedIn channels. The pitch is an IDE-style environment for creative work, which makes it relevant to anyone tracking how authoring tools for visual media are being designed.

item.title: [github_trending] cathrynlavery/diagram-design
item.description: cathrynlavery/diagram-design is an agent skill that renders diagrams as a single self-contained HTML + SVG file in your own brand, covering 44 diagram types and supporting Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Factory Droid and Pi. It deliberately drops shadows and avoids what the author calls Mermaid slop. Aimed at developers who need diagrams inside docs but find existing generators too templated.

item.title: [github_trending] bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view
item.description: God's Eye View is a browser-based spy-satellite simulator that layers live aircraft, ships, satellites, earthquakes, traffic and public camera feeds onto a photorealistic 3D globe, all from real open-source data, with hands-free voice control driven by a realtime AI agent. It comes from the viral YouTube series (formerly WorldView) with 5M+ views and reached #1 on GitHub Trending.

item.title: [github_trending] chrislgarry/Apollo-11
item.description: chrislgarry/Apollo-11 collects the original Apollo 11 Guidance Computer (AGC) source code for the command and lunar modules, and its README has been translated into dozens of languages including Chinese, Japanese, Russian and Hindi. It is a rare chance to read real 1960s flight-software assembly code, useful for anyone curious about early software engineering and spaceflight history.

item.title: [github_trending] lyogavin/airllm
item.description: AirLLM cuts inference memory so hard that a 70B model runs on a single 4GB GPU without quantization, distillation or pruning; per its README it also fits Kimi K3 (2.8T) under 4GB, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (125B) on 6GB and DeepSeek-V3 (671B) on roughly 12GB. It has added support for training large models on small VRAM, which matters to developers without big GPUs.

item.title: [github_trending] pytorch/pytorch
item.description: PyTorch is a Python package offering NumPy-like tensor computation with strong GPU acceleration plus deep neural networks built on a tape-based autograd system, and it interoperates with NumPy, SciPy and Cython. Its trunk CI health is published at hud.pytorch.org. It remains the framework most deep learning research and training code is built on.
